## Does Nigella sativa supplementation improve cardiovascular disease risk factors? A comprehensive GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of 82 randomized controlled trials
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/jafari-2025-40714301/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40714301/
Citation: Jafari A, Mardani H, Faghfouri AH, Fashtali ZM et al (2025), Pharmacological Research
- In Black seed oil (Nigella sativa): 82 studies (79 quantitative and 3 qualitative; the title calls them randomised controlled trials), 5,026 participants, 1 to 48 weeks (doses 200 to 4,600 mg a day) (n=5026). Nigella sativa supplementation significantly improved body fat percentage, systolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure, fasting blood sugar, HbA1c, post-meal glucose, insulin sensitivity, C-reactive protein, cholesterol fractions and triglycerides. The authors conclude it could be a promising adjunct therapy for improving cardiovascular risk factors.

## Immunological Outcomes of Bovine Colostrum Supplementation in Trained and Physically Active People: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/glowka-2020-32276466/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32276466/
Citation: Glowka N, Durkalec-Michalski K, Wozniewicz M (2020), Nutrients
- In Bovine colostrum supplements for immunity and gut health: Athletes and physically active adults in ten randomised trials of bovine colostrum (n=239). Bovine colostrum had no or only a fairly low effect on serum immunoglobulins (IgA, IgG), lymphocytes, neutrophils and saliva IgA. The authors note earlier work saying it reduces upper respiratory tract infections, and say the mechanism is unclear.

## Bovine Colostrum Applications in Sick and Healthy People: A Systematic Review
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/guberti-2021-34202206/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34202206/
Citation: Guberti M, Botti S, Capuzzo MT, Nardozi S et al (2021), Nutrients
- In Bovine colostrum supplements for immunity and gut health: Healthy and sick people in 28 papers (reviews, randomised trials, observational studies and case series) (n=28). Studies were highly varied in people, doses and risk of bias. As a supplement it showed "interesting effects" on upper respiratory illness in sportsmen, immune response and intestinal permeability. Results in children were conflicting, and there is little evidence in older adults.

## Bovine colostrum supplementation in rugby
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/mizelman-2026-40640599/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40640599/
Citation: Mizelman E, Shaw KA, Kaviani M, Brenna E et al (2026), European Journal of Applied Physiology
- In Bovine colostrum supplements for immunity and gut health: Club-level rugby players (26 men, 3 women), 8 weeks (n=29). Vertical jump height rose by about 1 cm with colostrum and fell by 0.5 cm with soy (p = 0.0023). There were no differences in upper or lower body strength, aerobic power, body composition, saliva immune markers or reported illness.

## Screening for Colorectal Cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/us-2021-34003218/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34003218/
Citation: US Preventive Services Task Force, Davidson KW, Barry MJ, Mangione CM et al (2021), JAMA
- In Bowel (colon) cancer screening: Asymptomatic adults aged 45 or over at average risk, US; the review also examined whether findings varied by age, sex or race/ethnicity (n=not stated in the abstract). High certainty that screening aged 50 to 75 has substantial net benefit; moderate certainty that screening at 45 to 49 has moderate net benefit. About 10.5% of new US colorectal cancers are in people under 50, and incidence in 40 to 49 year olds rose by almost 15% between 2000-2002 and 2014-2016. The abstract does not report results by race.

## Colorectal cancer statistics, 2023
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/siegel-2023-36856579/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36856579/
Citation: Siegel RL, Wagle NS, Cercek A, Smith RA et al (2023), CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians
- In Bowel (colon) cancer screening: US cancer statistics, all groups (n=national). In 2023 about 153,020 people in the US would be diagnosed and 52,550 would die; incidence is rising 1-2% a year in people under 55, and 60% of new cases were advanced in 2019. The abstract names mortality rising in Native Americans, not Black people, and gives no Black-specific rate.

## Hairdressing is associated with scalp disease in African schoolchildren
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/khumalo-2007-17553035/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17553035/
Citation: Khumalo NP et al (2007), British Journal of Dermatology
- In Braids, cornrows and twists for men and boys: 1,042 schoolchildren (45% boys), South Africa (n=1042). Acne keloidalis nuchae (neck bumps) was found in 0.67% overall and 4.7% of final-year boys, all with frequent haircuts; most boys (72.8%) kept natural hair with haircuts within 4 weeks. Traction alopecia was 9.4% overall and 17.1% in girls, and was more common with relaxed than natural hair; 8.6% of boys had relaxed hair.

## Epidemiology, Behavioral Determinants, Symptom Burden, and Severity of Traction Alopecia Among Ghanaian Women: A Cross-Sectional Study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/ayugane-2026-42953661/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42953661/
Citation: Ayugane et al (2026), Health Science Reports
- In Braids, twists and extensions: tension, how long, itch: 197 Ghanaian women, mean age 23, hairline status scored on the Marginal Traction Alopecia Score (n=197). 40.6% had hairline recession consistent with traction alopecia. More than two high-frequency heat-styling sessions a month was associated with higher odds (adjusted odds ratio 5.65, 95% CI 1.35-23.62). Keeping one hairstyle for over 6 weeks showed higher estimated odds that were not significant (1.81, 95% CI 0.59-5.60).
- In Heat, silk press, keratin treatments and colour: 197 Ghanaian women, mean age 23, hairline status scored on the Marginal Traction Alopecia Score (n=197). 40.6% had hairline recession consistent with traction alopecia. More than two high-frequency heat-styling sessions a month was associated with higher odds (adjusted odds ratio 5.65, 95% CI 1.35-23.62). Keeping one hairstyle for over 6 weeks showed higher estimated odds that were not significant (1.81, 95% CI 0.59-5.60).
- In Protecting your edges and hairline: 197 Ghanaian women, mean age 23, hairline status scored on the Marginal Traction Alopecia Score (n=197). 40.6% had hairline recession consistent with traction alopecia. More than two high-frequency heat-styling sessions a month was associated with higher odds (adjusted odds ratio 5.65, 95% CI 1.35-23.62). Keeping one hairstyle for over 6 weeks showed higher estimated odds that were not significant (1.81, 95% CI 0.59-5.60).

## Contact Sensitization to Allergens in Synthetic Hair and Related Hair Practices: A Review
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/collins-2025-39936215/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39936215/
Citation: Collins M, Yu J et al (2025), Dermatitis
- In Braids, twists and extensions: tension, how long, itch: Review of documented cases of contact dermatitis from synthetic hair and related practices (n=not stated). Synthetic hair extensions are known to cause contact dermatitis through allergens such as acrylates and disperse dyes. Scalp contact dermatitis can show up as itch, thinning or an eczema-like rash and is easily misdiagnosed. Braiding, wigs and the products used to maintain them are discussed.
- In Wigs, weaves and lace glue: Review of documented cases of contact dermatitis from synthetic hair and related practices (n=not stated). Synthetic hair extensions are known to cause contact dermatitis through allergens such as acrylates and disperse dyes. Scalp contact dermatitis can show up as itch, thinning or an eczema-like rash and is easily misdiagnosed. Braiding, wigs and the products used to maintain them are discussed.

## Early onset of breast cancer in a group of British black women
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/bowen-2008-18182985/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18182985/
Citation: Bowen RL, Duffy SW, Ryan DA, Hart IR et al (2008), British Journal of Cancer
- In Breast cancer, triple-negative disease and screening: Black and White women with invasive breast cancer, one East London hospital, 1994-2005 (n=not stated in the abstract). Black patients presented younger (median 46 years against 67 for White patients). Black women had more grade 3 tumours, lymph node-positive disease, hormone receptor-negative and basal-like (triple-negative) tumours. For tumours of 2 cm or less Black patients had poorer survival (hazard ratio 2.90, 95% CI 0.98-8.60, P=0.05). The authors say the findings could have major implications for detection and treatment.

## Breast cancer and age in Black and White women in South East England
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/jack-2012-21445965/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21445965/
Citation: Jack RH, Davies EA, Moller H (2012), International Journal of Cancer
- In Breast cancer, triple-negative disease and screening: Breast cancer cases among White, Black Caribbean and Black African women in South East England, 1998-2003 (n=not stated in the abstract). Black women had lower age-standardised incidence than White women. Under age 50 rates were similar across groups, and over 50 White women had higher rates. The younger age of Black patients reflects the younger age of the Black population, not a higher risk at younger ages.

## Short-term breast cancer survival in relation to ethnicity, stage, grade and receptor status: national cohort study in England
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/moller-2016-27780193/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27780193/
Citation: Moller H, Henson K, Luchtenborg M, Broggio J et al (2016), British Journal of Cancer
- In Breast cancer, triple-negative disease and screening: 86,852 women with breast cancer diagnosed in England 2012-2013 (n=86852). Triple-negative cancers had an adjusted hazard ratio for death of 2.00 (95% CI 1.84-2.17). Black women had an age-adjusted hazard ratio of 1.77 (1.48-2.13) against White women. The authors say the excess mortality has contributions from socio-economic factors, stage distribution and tumour biology.

## West African Genetic Ancestry and Breast Cancer Outcomes Among Black Women
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/reid-2024-39652347/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39652347/
Citation: Reid S, Fan R, Venton L, Weidner A et al (2024), JAMA Network Open
- In Breast cancer, triple-negative disease and screening: 687 Black women diagnosed with early-stage invasive breast cancer at age 50 or younger, Florida and Tennessee, 2005-2016 (n=687). Triple-negative disease and lymph node involvement were associated with shorter disease-free survival (hazard ratio 1.81 and 1.77). A higher percentage of West African genetic ancestry was associated with shorter survival in the hormone receptor-positive subgroup. Full-time employment was associated with better outcomes (hazard ratio 0.44).

## Effect of breathwork on stress and mental health: A meta-analysis of randomised-controlled trials
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/fincham-2023-36624160/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36624160/
Citation: Fincham GW, Strauss C, Montero-Marin J, Cavanagh K (2023), Scientific Reports
- In Breathwork and slow breathing: 785 adults in 12 randomised trials (various countries; ethnicity not given in the abstract) (n=785). Breathwork was associated with lower stress than control conditions (effect size g = -0.35, 95% CI -0.55 to -0.14). For anxiety (20 trials) g was -0.32 and for depressive symptoms (18 trials) -0.40. The authors urge caution to avoid a miscalibration between hype and evidence.

## Effect of breathing exercises on blood pressure and heart rate: A systematic review and meta-analysis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/garg-2024-38179185/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38179185/
Citation: Garg P, Mendiratta A, Banga A, Bucharles A et al (2024), International Journal of Cardiology: Cardiovascular Risk and Prevention
- In Breathwork and slow breathing: 15 randomised trials (hypertension and cardiovascular settings) (n=15 trials). Breathing exercises lowered systolic pressure by 7.06 mmHg (95% CI -10.20 to -3.92) and diastolic by 3.43 (-4.89 to -1.97), with a small fall in heart rate. The authors note the studies are not free of bias.

## Mindfulness in Motion and Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) in Hypertensive African Americans
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/wright-2021-33227157/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33227157/
Citation: Wright KD, Klatt MD, Adams IR, Nguyen CM et al (2021), Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
- In Breathwork and slow breathing: African American older adults with mild cognitive impairment and hypertension (pilot, US community centre) (n=not stated in the abstract). Feasible and culturally acceptable. Systolic blood pressure fell 7.2 mmHg in the intervention group against 0.7 in the attention-only group, but there was no difference from the true control group, and no changes in diet or mindfulness.

## Exploring effects of therapeutic massage and patient teaching in the practice of diaphragmatic breathing on blood pressure, stress, and anxiety in hypertensive African-American women: an intervention study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/jefferson-2010-20857772/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20857772/
Citation: Jefferson LL (2010), Journal of the National Black Nurses Association
- In Breathwork and slow breathing: African American women with hypertension (n=not stated). Systolic and diastolic pressure and an anxiety score fell significantly in the group one week after the massage intervention (P between .01 and .03). The abstract does not state randomisation or a comparison group.

## Mindfulness meditation lowers muscle sympathetic nerve activity and blood pressure in African-American males with chronic kidney disease
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/park-2014-24829497/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24829497/
Citation: Park J, Lyles RH, Bauer-Wu S (2014), American Journal of Physiology: Regulatory, Integrative and Comparative Physiology
- In Breathwork and slow breathing: 15 hypertensive African American men with chronic kidney disease (n=15). Mindfulness meditation lowered blood pressure, heart rate and muscle sympathetic nerve activity. Controlled breathing alone did not reduce blood pressure, heart rate or nerve activity in this study.
- In Meditation: 15 hypertensive African American men with chronic kidney disease (n=15). Mindfulness meditation acutely lowered systolic and diastolic pressure, heart rate and muscle sympathetic nerve activity compared with the control.

## Voluntary activation of the sympathetic nervous system and attenuation of the innate immune response in humans
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/kox-2014-24799686/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24799686/
Citation: Kox M et al (2014), Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
- In Breathwork and slow breathing: listed as a source, no finding recorded.

## Momordica charantia for type 2 diabetes mellitus
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/ooi-2012-22895968/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22895968/
Citation: Ooi CP, Yassin Z, Hamid TA (2012), Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
- In Bush teas and herbal remedies (cerasee, bitter leaf) with medicines: 479 adults with type 2 diabetes in four randomised trials of Momordica charantia (bitter gourd, cerasee) (n=4 trials (479 people)). No significant difference in glycaemic control against placebo, and none against metformin or glibenclamide in reliable measures. Risk of bias was generally high. No serious adverse effects were reported in any trial. The authors conclude there is insufficient evidence.
- In Type 2 diabetes risk and blood sugar: 479 adults with type 2 diabetes in four trials of Momordica charantia (bitter gourd, cerasee) (n=4 trials (479 people)). No significant difference in glycaemic control against placebo, and no significant change against metformin or glibenclamide in reliable measures. Risk of bias was generally high and only two trials were full peer-reviewed papers. The authors conclude there is insufficient evidence.

## A clinical trial of the traditional medicine Vernonia amygdalina in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/challand-2009-19922255/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19922255/
Citation: Challand S, Willcox M (2009), Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine
- In Bush teas and herbal remedies (cerasee, bitter leaf) with medicines: Patients aged 12 and over with uncomplicated malaria, a traditional remedy trial in Africa (n=not stated in the abstract). An adequate clinical response at day 14 occurred in 67% of cases, but complete parasite clearance occurred in only 32% of those, and 71% of those had recrudescence. No significant side effects or toxicity were seen. The authors say more studies are needed.

## A case of veno-occlusive disease of the liver in Britain associated with herbal tea consumption
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/mcgee-1976-977780/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/977780/
Citation: McGee J, Patrick RS, Wood CB, Blumgart LH (1976), Journal of Clinical Pathology
- In Bush teas and herbal remedies (cerasee, bitter leaf) with medicines: One young woman in Britain with liver disease linked to a herbal tea (n=1 patient). Veno-occlusive disease of the liver, similar to the condition occurring in the Caribbean, was diagnosed. Small amounts of pyrrolizidine alkaloids were recovered from the mate tea she drank heavily for years, and it seems probable that this caused the disease.

## Therapeutic Benefit of Vernonia amygdalina in the Treatment of Diabetes and Its Associated Complications in Preclinical Studies
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/asante-2023-38033739/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38033739/
Citation: Asante DB, Wiafe GA (2023), Journal of Diabetes Research
- In Bush teas and herbal remedies (cerasee, bitter leaf) with medicines: Diabetic rodents and cell and tissue models (preclinical review) (n=not applicable). The review calls bitter leaf potently antidiabetic in preclinical work and appraises the evidence for future research. All the studies discussed are in animals and cells.

## Vernonia amygdalina aqueous leaf extract modulates metformin pharmacokinetics, inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 enzymes in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/akowuah-2024-39710889/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39710889/
Citation: Akowuah GA, Sabbagh BA, Palanirajan VK, Chew YL et al (2024), Journal of Complementary and Integrative Medicine
- In Bush teas and herbal remedies (cerasee, bitter leaf) with medicines: Diabetic rats (4 groups of 6) and enzyme assays (n=24 rats). Given with metformin, the extract changed metformin's pharmacokinetics (higher peak level, higher total exposure and longer half-life) and inhibited the liver enzymes CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 in the assay. The authors say this suggests potential herb-drug interactions.

## The effects of sodium reduction and the DASH diet on ambulatory blood pressure: overall and race-stratified results from the DASH-Sodium trial
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/hussain-2026-42429484/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42429484/
Citation: Hussain T, Juraschek SP, Miller ER 3rd, Sacks FM et al (2026), American Journal of Hypertension
- In Caribbean and West African diets and health: 335 adults with ambulatory blood pressure data in the DASH-Sodium trial, 58% self-reported Black (n=335). Reducing sodium and consuming the DASH diet, alone or combined, significantly lowered 24-hour, awake and asleep blood pressure in Black and non-Black participants.
- In Salt and blood pressure: 335 adults with ambulatory blood pressure data in the DASH-Sodium feeding trial, 58% self-reported Black (n=335). Compared with the control diet at high sodium, reducing sodium and eating the DASH diet, alone or combined, significantly lowered 24-hour, awake and asleep blood pressure in Black and non-Black participants. The DASH diet with low sodium cut awake systolic pressure by 9.0 mmHg in Black and 7.5 in non-Black participants. Racial differences in achieved levels of asleep pressure persisted.

## Effects of dietary patterns on blood pressure: subgroup analysis of the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) randomized clinical trial
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/svetkey-1999-9989541/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9989541/
Citation: Svetkey LP, Simons-Morton D, Vollmer WM, Appel LJ et al (1999), Archives of Internal Medicine
- In Caribbean and West African diets and health: 459 adults in the original DASH trial (n=459). The combination diet lowered systolic blood pressure in all subgroups and was particularly effective in African Americans and people with hypertension.
- In Salt and blood pressure: 459 adults with untreated blood pressure below 160/80-95 in the original DASH feeding trial, subgroups analysed (n=459). The DASH combination diet, with weight and salt held constant, significantly lowered systolic blood pressure in all subgroups, and the authors say it was particularly effective in African Americans and in people with hypertension.

## Medical and environmental risk factors for the development of central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia: a population study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/kyei-2011-21482861/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21482861/
Citation: Kyei A, Bergfeld WF, Piliang M, Summers P (2011), Archives of Dermatology
- In CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown: 326 African American women at churches and a health fair, Cleveland (n=326). 28% scored as clinically evident central hair loss. Traction-associated hairstyles (braids and weaves) were associated with central scarring hair loss (P=.02), as were bacterial scalp infections and type 2 diabetes.
- In Traction alopecia and 'protective' styles: 326 African American women at churches and a health fair, Cleveland (n=326). 28% scored as clinically evident central hair loss. Traction-associated hairstyles (braids and weaves) were associated with central scarring hair loss (P=.02), as were bacterial scalp infections and type 2 diabetes.

## Variant PADI3 in Central Centrifugal Cicatricial Alopecia
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/malki-2019-30763140/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30763140/
Citation: Malki L et al (2019), New England Journal of Medicine
- In CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown: Patients with CCCA, two sets (n=not stated). PADI3 variants were found in 5 of 16 patients (31%) in the discovery set and in 9 of 42 in the replication set. Disease prevalence is given as up to 5.6%.

## Pathogenic variants affecting peptidyl arginine deiminase 3 and its major substrates underlie central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/keller-rosenthal-2026-41242654/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41242654/
Citation: Keller-Rosenthal et al (2026), Journal of Investigative Dermatology
- In CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown: 75 patients with CCCA (n=75). Nine pathogenic PADI3 variants were found, replicating the earlier signal.

## Prospective histologic examinations in patients who practice traumatic hairstyling
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/uhlenhake-2013-23452029/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23452029/
Citation: Uhlenhake E, Mehregan DR (2013), International Journal of Dermatology
- In CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown: 8 African American women with no clinical hair loss who used chemical or heat straighteners (n=8). Every biopsy showed inflammation around the follicle opening and a ring of fibrosis, with no follicle loss. The authors say these are findings characteristic of CCCA and suggest a histological prelude, and that CCCA may be a common pathway of inflammation and scarring that traumatic hairstyling can set off in genetically predisposed people.
- In Heat, silk press, keratin treatments and colour: 8 African American women with no clinical hair loss who used chemical or heat straighteners (n=8). Every biopsy showed inflammation around the follicle opening and a ring of fibrosis, with no follicle loss. The authors say these are findings characteristic of CCCA and suggest a histological prelude, and that CCCA may be a common pathway of inflammation and scarring that traumatic hairstyling can set off in genetically predisposed people.

## Scarring Alopecias Part 2: Treatments
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/ajmani-2026-43009060/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43009060/
Citation: Ajmani S, Klufas D et al (2026), Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
- In CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown: Review of scarring alopecias (n=not stated). There are no FDA-approved therapies for primary scarring alopecias; all treatments are off label. Lymphocytic types including CCCA may respond to immunomodulatory agents, and the aims are to halt inflammation, relieve symptoms and preserve follicles. Minoxidil and similar agents are used as camouflage.

## Central Centrifugal Cicatricial Alopecia in Black Women: Diagnostic Challenges and Molecular Insights
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/persson-2026-42910370/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42910370/
Citation: Persson et al (2026), Cureus
- In CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown: Review of 15 primary studies, 2015 to 2025 (n=15). CCCA mostly presents as progressive thinning of the central scalp, may resemble androgenetic alopecia or alopecia areata, and is underrecognised and often misdiagnosed. Dermoscopy and biopsy remain important.
- In Finding a stylist, trichologist or dermatologist who knows afro hair: Review of 15 primary studies, 2015 to 2025 (n=15). CCCA mostly presents as progressive thinning of the central scalp, may resemble androgenetic alopecia or alopecia areata, and is underrecognised and often misdiagnosed. Dermoscopy and biopsy remain important.

## Central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia in males
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/jackson-2023-37495175/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37495175/
Citation: Jackson et al (2023), Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
- In CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown: 17 men with biopsy-confirmed CCCA, one US academic centre, 2012 to 2022 (n=17). Average age 43; 88.2% identified as Black. Scalp itch was the commonest symptom; few reported high-risk hair practices; none had type 2 diabetes. The authors say CCCA should be considered in adult Black men with hair loss.
- In Receding hairline and hair transplants in Black men: 17 men with biopsy-confirmed CCCA, one US academic centre, 2012 to 2022 (n=17). Average age 43; 88.2% identified as Black. Scalp itch was the commonest symptom; few reported high-risk hair practices; none had type 2 diabetes. The authors say CCCA should be considered in adult Black men with hair loss.

## A phase 2a trial of brepocitinib for cicatricial alopecia
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/david-2025-39461505/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39461505/
Citation: David E, Shokrian N, Del Duca E, Meariman M et al (2025), Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
- In CCCA: scarring hair loss at the crown: Adults with lichen planopilaris, frontal fibrosing alopecia or central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia (how many had CCCA is not stated in the abstract) (n=not stated in the abstract). Brepocitinib significantly lowered lesional CCL5 expression at week 24 (P=.004), was well tolerated and improved clinical severity scores. Coprimary endpoints were biomarkers and safety, not hair regrowth. The authors list a single dose and a small placebo group as limitations.

## Use of Straighteners and Other Hair Products and Incident Uterine Cancer
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/chang-2022-36245087/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36245087/
Citation: Chang CJ, O'Brien KM, Keil AP, Gaston SA et al (2022), Journal of the National Cancer Institute
- In Chemical relaxers and hair straighteners: 33,947 US women aged 35-74 in the Sister Study (racially and ethnically diverse) (n=33947). Ever use of straightening products in the previous year was associated with higher uterine cancer rates (hazard ratio 1.80, 95% CI 1.12-2.88); more than 4 uses in the previous year, 2.55 (1.46-4.45). Dyes and perms were not associated. The authors call it the first epidemiological evidence of this link and say more research is warranted.

## Hair relaxer use and risk of uterine cancer in the Black Women's Health Study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/bertrand-2023-37821068/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37821068/
Citation: Bertrand KA, Delp L, Coogan PF, Cozier YC et al (2023), Environmental Research
- In Chemical relaxers and hair straighteners: 44,798 Black women with an intact uterus in the Black Women's Health Study; 347 uterine cancers (n=44798). Heavy use (15 or more years, at least 5 times a year) against never or light use gave a hazard ratio of 1.18 (95% CI 0.81-1.71), not significant. Among postmenopausal women, heavy use was 1.64 (1.01-2.64) and 20 or more years of use 1.71 (1.08-2.72). Premenopausal women: null.

## Hair product use and breast cancer incidence in the Black Women's Health Study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/coogan-2021-34013957/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34013957/
Citation: Coogan PF, Rosenberg L, Palmer JR, Cozier YC et al (2021), Carcinogenesis
- In Chemical relaxers and hair straighteners: 50,543 Black women, Black Women's Health Study; 2,311 breast cancers (n=50543). Heavy use of relaxers gave a hazard ratio for breast cancer of 1.13 (95% CI 0.96-1.33), not significant. For heavy use of lye-containing relaxers the hazard ratio for ER-positive breast cancer was 1.32 (0.97-1.80), also not significant. The authors call the results largely null.

## Hair relaxer use and risk of uterine leiomyomata in African-American women
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/wise-2012-22234483/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22234483/
Citation: Wise LA, Palmer JR, Reich D, Cozier YC et al (2012), American Journal of Epidemiology
- In Chemical relaxers and hair straighteners: 23,580 premenopausal Black women, Black Women's Health Study; 7,146 fibroid cases (n=23580). Ever against never use of relaxers: incidence rate ratio 1.17 (95% CI 1.06-1.30), with trends for frequency, duration and number of scalp burns. The authors say the findings raise the hypothesis that relaxer use increases fibroid risk.
- In Iron, heavy periods and fibroids: 23,580 premenopausal Black women, Black Women's Health Study (n=23580). Ever against never relaxer use: incidence rate ratio 1.17 (95% CI 1.06-1.30); the authors raise this as a hypothesis.
- In Relaxer, texturiser, perm and keratin: what is the difference: 23,580 premenopausal Black women, Black Women's Health Study; 7,146 fibroid cases (n=23580). Ever against never use of relaxers: incidence rate ratio 1.17 (95% CI 1.06-1.30), with trends for frequency, duration and number of scalp burns. The authors say the findings raise the hypothesis that relaxer use increases fibroid risk.

## Systematic Review of the Epidemiology of Hair Relaxer Use and Hormone-Sensitive Reproductive Outcomes Among Black Adult Women in the United States
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/hernandez-2025-39828620/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39828620/
Citation: Hernandez AM, Smith SJ, Vahora MS, Campbell D et al (2025), Journal of Applied Toxicology
- In Chemical relaxers and hair straighteners: Seven cohort studies and one case-control study in US Black women (n=8 studies). The authors conclude that the weight of the evidence does not support relaxers being a risk factor for gynaecological and breast cancers in US Black women. They note one study found a statistically significant link with fibroids and that none of the studies characterised the chemical constituents.

## Prevalence of Adverse Childhood Experiences From the 2011-2014 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System in 23 States
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/merrick-2018-30242348/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30242348/
Citation: Merrick MT, Ford DC, Ports KA, Guinn AS (2018), JAMA Pediatrics
- In Childhood trauma and where to start: 214,157 adults in 23 US states in the 2011 to 2014 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (n=214157). 61.55% had at least 1 ACE and 24.64% reported 3 or more. Higher ACE scores were reported by people who identified as Black (mean 1.69, 95% CI 1.62 to 1.76), Hispanic (1.80) or multiracial (2.52), and by those with lower income, education and employment, and by gay, lesbian or bisexual people.

## Cumulative adverse childhood experiences and risk of mental disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/annor-2026-42066531/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42066531/
Citation: Annor E, Pollak M, Ramasamy D (2026), Acta Psychologica
- In Childhood trauma and where to start: 56 studies (40 in the meta-analysis) of cumulative adverse childhood experiences and mental disorders (n=56). Cumulative ACEs were strongly associated with mental disorders (pooled odds ratio 3.18, 95% CI 2.84 to 3.56) with a dose-response gradient from 1 to 4 or more ACEs. Findings were robust in sensitivity tests with minimal publication bias; the authors call for trauma-informed care and global equity in ACE research.

## Psychological therapies for children and adolescents exposed to trauma
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/gillies-2016-27726123/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27726123/
Citation: Gillies D, Maiocchi L, Bhandari AP, Taylor F et al (2016), Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
- In Childhood trauma and where to start: 51 randomised trials with 6,201 children and adolescents who had been exposed to trauma (sexual abuse in 12 trials, war or community violence in 10, other traumas in the rest) (n=6201). Psychological therapy cut the chance of a PTSD diagnosis, compared with no treatment, usual care or waiting list, for up to a month after therapy (odds ratio 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 to 0.77). Seventeen trials used cognitive-behavioural therapy and two EMDR.

## Childhood Adversity and Anxiety, Depression, and Suicidal Behaviors Among African-Origin Emerging Adults in the United States: Findings From an Online Panel
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/byansi-2026-42841399/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42841399/
Citation: Byansi W, Williamson E, Peoples JE, Motley RO et al (2026), Journal of Community Psychology
- In Childhood trauma and where to start: 537 African-origin emerging adults aged 18 to 29 in the United States (first- and second-generation) (n=537). Higher ACE scores were associated with more anxiety and depressive symptoms and higher odds of lifetime suicidal ideation and suicide attempt. Associations were stronger for suicidal ideation and attempt in first-generation participants. The authors support culturally responsive, trauma-informed assessment and intervention.

## The impact of adverse childhood experiences on the development of multimorbidity in older adults in Nigeria
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/ahmed-2026-42789523/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42789523/
Citation: Ahmed A, Khan HTA, Asiamah N (2026), PLoS One
- In Childhood trauma and where to start: 734 adults aged 60 and over in Niger State, North-Central Nigeria (n=734). 68.4% reported 4 or more ACEs, and 38.4% had three or more chronic conditions. After adjustment, cumulative ACEs remained an independent predictor of multimorbidity (odds ratio 15.58, 95% CI 1.33 to 182.21).

## Scarring Alopecia Management and Referral Practices in African-American Cosmetologists
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/onamusi-2025-40654542/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40654542/
Citation: Onamusi T et al (2025), International Journal of Trichology
- In Choosing a stylist, braider or loctician: 19 African-American cosmetologists, US (n=19). 78.9% had never heard of lichen planopilaris and 57.9% had never heard of CCCA. All reported avoiding or limiting tight braids or locs and tight ponytails or buns; 89.5% avoided tight weaves. 94.7% (18 of 19) had referred a client to a dermatologist in the past year. The authors say there are gaps in knowledge of hair loss risk factors.

## Prevention of covid-19 and other acute respiratory infections with cod liver oil supplementation, a low dose vitamin D supplement: quadruple blinded, randomised placebo controlled trial
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/brunvoll-2022-36215222/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36215222/
Citation: Brunvoll SH, Nygaard AB, Ellingjord-Dale M, Holland P et al (2022), BMJ
- In Cod liver oil: vitamin D, vitamin A and colds: 34,601 adults aged 18 to 75 in Norway not taking daily vitamin D (n=34,601). Cod liver oil did not reduce the risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection, serious covid-19, or other acute respiratory infections (for example any acute respiratory infection, relative risk 1.04, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.11). Only low-grade side effects were reported.

## Cod liver oil, young children, and upper respiratory tract infections
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/linday-2010-21677119/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21677119/
Citation: Linday LA (2010), Journal of the American College of Nutrition
- In Cod liver oil: vitamin D, vitamin A and colds: Young children (US, low-income; details not given in the abstract) (n=not stated). The author reports that these supplements cut winter and spring visits for upper respiratory illness by 36% to 58%. The paper notes cod liver oil is culturally valued and has been a folk remedy among many low-income minorities in the United States.

## Effects of Oral Collagen for Skin Anti-Aging: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/pu-2023-37432180/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37432180/
Citation: Pu SY, Huang YL, Pu CM, Kang YN et al (2023), Nutrients
- In Collagen supplements for skin and joints: Adults in 26 randomised trials of hydrolysed collagen for skin (n=1721). Collagen supplements improved skin hydration and elasticity compared with placebo. Effects on hydration varied by collagen source and length of use. The authors note several biases in the included trials and call for larger trials.

## Effects of Collagen Supplements on Skin Aging: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/myung-2025-40324552/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40324552/
Citation: Myung SK, Park Y (2025), American Journal of Medicine
- In Collagen supplements for skin and joints: Adults in 23 randomised trials of collagen supplements for skin ageing (n=1474). Across all trials, collagen improved hydration, elasticity and wrinkles. Trials not funded by pharmaceutical companies found no effect, as did high-quality trials, while industry-funded and low-quality trials found benefit. The authors conclude there is currently no clinical evidence to support collagen supplements to prevent or treat skin ageing.

## Chemical and physical treatments damage Caucasian and Afro-ethnic hair fibre: analytical and image assays
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/bloch-2019-31237371/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31237371/
Citation: Bloch et al (2019), Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology
- In Colouring and bleaching afro-textured hair: Caucasian (straight, wavy, curly) and Afro-ethnic hair tresses (n=not stated). Bleaching, dyeing and UV light increased the combing work of afro-ethnic tresses, indicating cuticle damage confirmed by electron microscopy. Bleaching and dyeing caused wear on cuticles with high protein loss whatever the curliness. Thioglycolate straightening faded brown and black tresses.
- In Heat, silk press, keratin treatments and colour: Caucasian (straight, wavy, curly) and Afro-ethnic hair tresses (n=not stated). Bleaching, dyeing and UV light increased the combing work of afro-ethnic tresses, indicating cuticle damage confirmed by electron microscopy. Bleaching and dyeing caused wear on cuticles with high protein loss whatever the curliness. Thioglycolate straightening faded brown and black tresses.
- In Relaxer, texturiser, perm and keratin: what is the difference: Caucasian (straight, wavy, curly) and Afro-ethnic hair tresses (n=not stated). Bleaching, dyeing and UV light increased the combing work of afro-ethnic tresses, indicating cuticle damage confirmed by electron microscopy. Bleaching and dyeing caused wear on cuticles with high protein loss whatever the curliness. Thioglycolate straightening faded brown and black tresses.

## Raman spectroscopy and electronic microscopy structural studies of Caucasian and Afro human hair
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/dos-2019-31111104/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31111104/
Citation: Dos Santos et al (2019), Heliyon
- In Colouring and bleaching afro-textured hair: Caucasian and Afro hair samples, treated with heat, bleach and straightening alone and together (n=not stated). Bleaching, straightening and heat changed chemical bonds and protein structure; excessive heat caused the largest change, and applying several treatments to the same fibres caused even more pronounced changes. The two hair groups showed small differences for each treatment.

## Patch Testing to Paraphenylenediamine: The North American Contact Dermatitis Group Experience (1994-2018)
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/warshaw-2023-37523239/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37523239/
Citation: Warshaw EM et al (2023), Dermatitis
- In Colouring and bleaching afro-textured hair: 54,917 patients patch tested to paraphenylenediamine (PPD) by the North American Contact Dermatitis Group, 1994-2018 (n=54917). 3,095 (5.6%) had an allergic reaction to PPD; hair dye was the source in 73.5%. Allergic patients had lower odds of being White (odds ratio 0.66) and higher odds of being over 40 and female. Of occupational reactions (8.3%), 72.8% were in hairdressers or cosmetologists.

## Perceived colorism and lifetime psychiatric disorders among Black American adults: findings from the National Survey of American Life
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/oh-2021-33961079/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33961079/
Citation: Oh H, Lincoln K, Waldman K (2021), Social Psychiatry and Psychiatric Epidemiology
- In Colourism, skin tone and mental health: Black American adults, National Survey of American Life 2001-2003 (probability sample) (n=not stated in the abstract). In-group colourism (from other Black people) was associated with greater odds of any lifetime psychiatric disorder (aOR 1.20, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.32); out-group colourism was not (aOR 1.08, 0.99 to 1.18). In-group colourism was linked to alcohol use, substance use, anxiety and eating disorders, but not PTSD or mood disorder. The authors say more research is needed to understand why.

## How Skin Tone Influences Relationships Between Discrimination, Psychological Distress, and Self-Rated Mental Health Among Older African Americans
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/hamler-2022-35976084/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35976084/
Citation: Hamler TC, Nguyen AW, Keith V, Qin W et al (2022), Journals of Gerontology Series B
- In Colourism, skin tone and mental health: 837 African Americans aged 55 or over, National Survey of American Life (n=837). Discrimination was linked to worse self-rated mental health and serious psychological distress, and the link with distress was stronger in darker-skinned respondents than lighter ones. For self-rated mental health the skin tone effect held for men but not women.

## Colorism and Health Inequities among Black Americans: A Biopsychosocial Perspective
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/dennis-2026-40981000/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40981000/
Citation: Dennis AC, DeAngelis R, Hargrove TW, Pearson JA (2026), Journal of Health and Social Behavior
- In Colourism, skin tone and mental health: 627 working-age Black adults in Nashville, 2011-2014 (n=627). Black adults who perceived themselves as dark-skinned had a lower sense of mattering and shorter telomeres than those who perceived their skin lighter, regardless of interviewer-rated skin tone.

## Racial/ethnic matching of clients and therapists in mental health services: a meta-analytic review of preferences, perceptions, and outcomes
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/cabral-2011-21875181/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21875181/
Citation: Cabral RR, Smith TB (2011), Journal of Counseling Psychology
- In Colourism, skin tone and mental health: Clients and therapists across 52 to 81 studies per question; countries not stated in the abstract (n=52 preference, 81 perception, 53 outcome studies). Matching made almost no difference to treatment outcomes on average (d 0.09), despite a moderately strong preference for a matched therapist (d 0.63). Studies with African American participants had the highest effect sizes.
- In Finding a Black therapist or one who understands being Black: Clients and therapists across 52 to 81 studies per question; countries not stated in the abstract (n=52 preference, 81 perception, 53 outcome studies). People preferred a therapist of their own race or ethnicity (d 0.63, moderately strong) and rated them somewhat more positively (d 0.32), but matching made almost no difference to treatment outcomes on average (d 0.09). Effects varied a lot between studies, and studies with African American participants had the highest effect sizes on all three.

## Effects of Creatine Supplementation and Resistance Training on Muscle Strength Gains in Adults <50 Years of Age: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/wang-2024-39519498/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39519498/
Citation: Wang Z, Qiu B, Li R, Han Y et al (2024), Nutrients
- In Creatine supplements: strength, kidneys and your kidney test: Adults under 50 in 23 trials of creatine with resistance training (460 men and 49 women across the included studies) (n=509). Creatine with resistance training raised upper-body strength by 4.4 kg and lower-body strength by 11.4 kg more than placebo. Males gained strength; females showed no significant gains, though only three studies included women. Ethnicity was not reported.

## Effect of creatine supplementation on kidney function: a systematic review and meta-analysis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/naeini-2025-41199218/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41199218/
Citation: Naeini EK, Eskandari M, Mortazavi M, Gholaminejad A et al (2025), BMC Nephrology
- In Creatine supplements: strength, kidneys and your kidney test: Adults in 21 studies (12 in the creatinine meta-analysis: 177 on creatine, 263 controls) (n=440). Creatine produced a small, statistically significant rise in serum creatinine, with no significant change in glomerular filtration rate (GFR). The authors call the creatinine rise modest and probably due to metabolic turnover with no sign of kidney impairment.

## Impact of African-enriched GATM regulatory variants on creatinine-derived estimated glomerular filtration rate
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/gray-2026-42498056/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42498056/
Citation: Gray OA, Yerges-Armstrong L, Castel SE, Brandenburg JT et al (2026), Kidney International
- In Creatine supplements: strength, kidneys and your kidney test: People in population cohorts in Uganda (5,760) and South Africa (827), checked in African American participants of the Million Veteran Program (n=6587). Variants in the GATM gene, common in African populations (allele frequency about 50 per cent) and rare in Europeans, raise creatine production and so serum creatinine. Each copy lowers the creatinine-based kidney estimate (eGFR) by about 2 mL/min/1.73 m2 with no link to measured GFR or cystatin C, so the estimate can read low without kidney disease.

## Treatments of Periorbital Hyperpigmentation: A Systematic Review
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/michelle-2021-32740208/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32740208/
Citation: Michelle L, Pouldar Foulad D, Ekelem C et al (2021), Dermatologic Surgery
- In Dark circles under the eyes: Participants in 39 studies of periorbital hyperpigmentation; groups not stated in the abstract (n=39). Fillers and fat grafting work best for dark circles from volume loss; blepharoplasty for loose skin; creams and peels for pigment; lasers mildly to moderately for vascular and pigment types. The authors note the scarcity of high-quality evidence and ask for more randomised trials.

## Topical tretinoin (retinoic acid) therapy for hyperpigmented lesions caused by inflammation of the skin in black patients
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/bulengo-ransby-1993-8479462/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8479462/
Citation: Bulengo-Ransby SM, Griffiths CE, Kimbrough-Green CK, Finkel LJ et al (1993), New England Journal of Medicine
- In Dark marks after acne (post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation): 54 Black adults with post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation who completed the study (n=54). Facial lesions in the tretinoin group were significantly lighter than vehicle (P<0.001). Colorimetry showed 40% lightening of lesions against 18% with vehicle (P=0.05). Improvement began after about 4 weeks. Retinoid dermatitis developed in 12 of 24 tretinoin-treated people (50%) but eased with time. Tretinoin lightened normal skin slightly.

## Postinflammatory hyperpigmentation: a review of the epidemiology, clinical features, and treatment options in skin of color
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/davis-2010-20725554/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20725554/
Citation: Davis EC, Callender VD (2010), Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology
- In Dark marks after acne (post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation): Review of treatment options in skin of colour (n=not stated). Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation tends to affect darker skin more often and more severely. Treatment should begin early, starting with management of the original inflammation. First-line therapy is typically topical depigmenting agents plus photoprotection including sunscreen. The authors warn to use caution with all treatments to avoid irritation and worsening of the pigmentation.

## Efficacy and Safety of Fixed-dose Clindamycin Phosphate 1.2%/Adapalene 0.15%/Benzoyl Peroxide 3.1% Gel in Black Participants with Moderate to Severe Acne
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/callender-2025-40256338/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40256338/
Citation: Callender VD, Alexis AF, Bhatia N, Harper JC et al (2025), Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology
- In Dark marks after acne (post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation): 156 Black participants (14% of 1,115) pooled from four industry trials in acne (n=156). Acne treatment success was 32.0% against 18.3% on vehicle (P=0.07). Inflammatory and noninflammatory lesions fell more with the gel, and hyperpigmentation scores stayed at or below baseline. The authors state the studies were not powered for Black participants, so P values are informative only.

## Impact of long-wavelength UVA and visible light on melanocompetent skin
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/mahmoud-2010-20410914/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20410914/
Citation: Mahmoud BH, Ruvolo E, Hexsel CL, Liu Y et al (2010), Journal of Investigative Dermatology
- In Dark marks after acne (post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation): People with skin types IV-VI (n=20). In normal lower-back skin of 20 volunteers, visible light induced darker and more sustained pigmentation than UVA1 in skin types IV-VI. Existing marks were not tested.
- In Sunscreen on dark skin: 20 volunteers with skin types IV-VI, plus skin type II for comparison (n=20). Both UVA1 and visible light induced pigmentation in skin types IV-VI. Pigmentation from visible light was darker and more sustained. No pigmentation was seen in skin type II.

## The Efficacy and Safety of a 755-nm Picosecond Laser in the Treatment of Physiologic Lip Hyperpigmentation in Thai Patients
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/ng-2022-36037096/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36037096/
Citation: Ng JNC, Manuskiatti W, Apinuntham C, Yan C (2022), Dermatologic Surgery
- In Dark or swollen lips: 20 healthy Thai adults with physiologic lip hyperpigmentation (n=20). Average melanin index fell significantly after the fourth treatment and at 1 month, and 70% of patients reported moderate to marked improvement at 6 months. One patient had a transient lip swelling. The authors describe physiologic lip hyperpigmentation as a common aesthetic concern, especially in Southeast Asia.

## Oral melanin pigmentation in smoked and smokeless tobacco users in India. Clinico-pathological study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/sarswathi-2003-14705454/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14705454/
Citation: Sarswathi TR, Kumar SN, Kavitha KM (2003), Indian Journal of Dental Research
- In Dark or swollen lips: 41 tobacco users and 8 controls in India (n=49). In smokers, 95.24% had pigmentation of the lip and cheek lining, the lip more (81%) than the cheek (33.3%), with more melanocytes on tissue examination. Pigmentation was absent at the site where smokeless tobacco was held.

## Pigmented contact cheilitis: a systematic review
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/figueiredo-2024-39396149/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39396149/
Citation: Figueiredo AS, Braz GL, Garcia FF, Moreno LB et al (2024), Medicina Oral, Patologia Oral y Cirugia Bucal
- In Dark or swollen lips: 7 reported cases of pigmented contact cheilitis (6 women, mean age 32) (n=7 cases). Ricinoleic acid and gum ester were the most frequent allergens, each in two cases. All cases had multiple pigmented lesions, with itching, scaling, swelling, redness, vesicles or papules, and a mean duration of 13.5 months. The authors say it often alarms patients because of the unexpected darkening.

## Labial melanotic macule: a clinical, histopathologic, and ultrastructural study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/ho-1993-8425968/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8425968/
Citation: Ho KK, Dervan P, O'Loughlin S, Powell FC (1993), Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology
- In Dark or swollen lips: 29 patients with 36 labial melanotic macules (n=29). The labial melanotic macule is a distinctive benign pigment spot, usually a single lesion on the lower lip, starting around age 30, mostly in women. It can simulate malignant melanoma, and the tissue testing supported its benign nature.

## Hyperinsulinemia and acanthosis nigricans in African Americans
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/stuart-1997-9264219/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9264219/
Citation: Stuart CA, Gilkison CR, Keenan BS, Nagamani M (1997), Journal of the National Medical Association
- In Dark velvety patches on the neck and folds (acanthosis nigricans): 89 African American people with acanthosis nigricans and 25 without (n=114). Diabetes was present in 19 of those with acanthosis nigricans, reaching 50% among those in their 40s. Fasting insulin rose in direct proportion to the severity of neck involvement. The authors read the skin sign as a marker of hyperinsulinaemia and insulin resistance.

## Association of diet with acne vulgaris among adolescents in Ibadan, southwest Nigeria
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/okoro-2016-26749364/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26749364/
Citation: Okoro EO, Ogunbiyi AO, George AO, Subulade MO (2016), International Journal of Dermatology
- In Does diet cause acne? Sugar, dairy and foods linked to spots: 464 adolescents (mean age 13.6) in schools in Ibadan, southwest Nigeria; 64.4% had acne (n=464). Acne was more common in students who reported at least daily milk as a drink (72.6% vs 62.0%), corn (76.6% vs 62.3%), fried beef (75.0% vs 62.1%) and cake (77.8% vs 62.3%), and less common with daily bananas (55.3% vs 67.6%). The authors say an interventional dietary study is needed.

## Diet and acne: A systematic review
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/meixiong-2022-35373155/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35373155/
Citation: Meixiong J, Ricco C, Vasavda C, Ho BK (2022), JAAD International
- In Does diet cause acne? Sugar, dairy and foods linked to spots: Mixed populations in 34 included studies (Ottawa quality scale) (n=34 articles). High glycaemic index and glycaemic load and carbohydrate intake were positively associated with acne and its severity, and this was supported by randomised trials. The dairy literature is mixed and may depend on sex, ethnicity and cultural dietary habits. The authors call the effect modest and say further trials are needed.

## A low-glycemic-load diet improves symptoms in acne vulgaris patients: a randomized controlled trial
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/smith-2007-17616769/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17616769/
Citation: Smith RN, Mann NJ, Braue A, Makelainen H et al (2007), American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
- In Does diet cause acne? Sugar, dairy and foods linked to spots: 43 male acne patients aged 15 to 25 in Australia (n=43). Total lesion counts fell more with the low-glycaemic-load diet (-23.5 vs -12.0, P=0.03). Weight and insulin sensitivity also improved more, so the authors say weight loss and diet effects cannot be separated.

## Dairy Intake and Acne Vulgaris: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 78,529 Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/juhl-2018-30096883/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30096883/
Citation: Juhl CR, Bergholdt HKM, Miller IM, Jemec GBE et al (2018), Nutrients
- In Does diet cause acne? Sugar, dairy and foods linked to spots: 78,529 children, adolescents and young adults aged 7 to 30 in 14 observational studies (n=14 studies (78,529 people)). Any dairy, milk, yogurt and cheese were each associated with higher odds of acne (for example any dairy OR 1.25, 95% CI 1.15 to 1.36). Adjusted results were smaller, there was publication bias and heterogeneity, and the authors say results should be read with caution.

## The mediterranean diet and acne vulgaris: a systematic review and meta-analysis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/taha-2025-41194132/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41194132/
Citation: Taha S, Shakhshir M, Zyoud SH (2025), Nutrition and Metabolism
- In Does diet cause acne? Sugar, dairy and foods linked to spots: 765 participants in five case-control studies (n=5 studies (765 people)). Closer adherence to the Mediterranean diet was linked to less severe acne but not significantly to lower odds of developing acne, and quality of evidence was low. More vegetables were linked to lower odds of acne.

## Topical antifungals for seborrhoeic dermatitis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/okokon-2015-25933684/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25933684/
Citation: Okokon EO, Verbeek JH et al (2015), Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
- In Dry, itchy, flaky scalp and dandruff: Adolescents and adults with seborrhoeic dermatitis of the face or scalp, randomised trials in mixed populations (n=not stated). Topical ketoconazole 2% gave a 31% lower risk of failed clearance than placebo at four weeks (risk ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.59-0.81, low-quality evidence), a remission rate similar to steroids with fewer side effects, and results similar to ciclopirox. The authors note that 24 trials appeared to have conflicts of interest such as pharmaceutical funding.

## High Curl Pattern Hair and Scalp Care Considerations to Mitigate Seborrheic Dermatitis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/callender-2026-41998807/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41998807/
Citation: Callender VD, Burgess C et al (2026), Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology
- In Dry, itchy, flaky scalp and dandruff: Consensus panel of dermatologists on high-curl-pattern hair and seborrhoeic dermatitis (n=not stated). High-curl-pattern hair is said to be more susceptible to breakage and to seborrhoeic dermatitis, and some common hair care practices may contribute to or worsen it. The panel says ceramide-containing products may help scalp barrier health.

## Current Understanding of Seborrheic Dermatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Special Populations
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/turchin-2025-40965095/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40965095/
Citation: Turchin I, Albrecht J et al (2025), Journal of Cutaneous Medicine and Surgery
- In Dry, itchy, flaky scalp and dandruff: Review of seborrhoeic dermatitis in different populations (n=not stated). In people with more richly pigmented skin, post-inflammatory pigment change can be a feature of seborrhoeic dermatitis, so skin colour matters for diagnosis; it overlaps with atopic dermatitis, psoriasis and rosacea.

## An epidemic of pediculosis capitis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/slonka-1977-870674/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/870674/
Citation: Slonka GF, Fleissner ML et al (1977), Journal of Parasitology
- In Dry, itchy, flaky scalp and dandruff: School pupils in Buffalo, New York, 1972 to 1973 (n=not stated). In one elementary school 20% of white pupils and no Black pupils were infested; city-wide 7.2% of pupils were infested. Hair length was apparently not a factor.
- In Head lice in afro-textured hair and locs: School pupils in Buffalo, New York, 1972 to 1973 (n=not stated). In one elementary school 20% of white pupils and no Black pupils were infested; city-wide 7.2% of pupils were infested. Hair length was apparently not a factor.

## Pediculosis in a school population
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/estrada-2000-11885087/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11885087/
Citation: Estrada B, Morris R (2000), Journal of School Nursing
- In Dry, itchy, flaky scalp and dandruff: School children, elementary to high school (US) (n=not stated). Hispanic children had the highest rate of infestation, then Caucasian children. African American children showed a 15% infestation rate, which the authors say is not supported by other studies.
- In Head lice in afro-textured hair and locs: School children, elementary to high school (US) (n=not stated). Hispanic children had the highest rate of infestation, then Caucasian children. African American children showed a 15% infestation rate, which the authors say is not supported by other studies.

## Tapinarof Cream for Adults and Children with Atopic Dermatitis-Efficacy by Race and Fitzpatrick Skin Type in Two Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trials
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/alexis-2025-40696240/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40696240/
Citation: Alexis AF, Kircik L, Chovatiya R et al (2025), Dermatology and Therapy
- In Eczema on dark skin (atopic eczema, including babies): Adults and children with atopic dermatitis in two US trials; about a quarter to a third Black or African American, over half Fitzpatrick IV-VI (n=813). In both trials more people on tapinarof than on vehicle reached clear or almost clear skin, in every race group. Black or African American: 43.1-47.0% on tapinarof against 17.5-24.1% on vehicle. White: 49.4-52.1% against 12.2-14.5%.

## Atopic dermatitis in diverse racial and ethnic groups-Variations in epidemiology, genetics, clinical presentation and treatment
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/kaufman-2018-29457272/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29457272/
Citation: Kaufman BP, Guttman-Yassky E, Alexis AF (2018), Experimental Dermatology
- In Eczema on dark skin (atopic eczema, including babies): Literature on atopic dermatitis in non-White groups (n=not stated). Atopic dermatitis occurs more often in Asian and Black people than in White people, studies are mostly in people of European ancestry, and the clinical features in non-White groups are underappreciated. The abstract does not list the features.

## Atopic dermatitis in African American children: addressing unmet needs of a common disease
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/vachiramon-2012-22471955/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22471955/
Citation: Vachiramon V, Tey HL, Thompson AE, Yosipovitch G (2012), Pediatric Dermatology
- In Eczema on dark skin (atopic eczema, including babies): African American children with atopic dermatitis (n=not stated). Prevalence in African American children is reported as significantly higher than in Caucasians, and the presentation seems to differ, but there is little information. The abstract does not list the differences.

## Effects of Ramadan Fasting on Glycaemic Control Among Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Observational Studies
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/elmajnoun-2023-36725794/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36725794/
Citation: Elmajnoun HK, Faris ME, Abdelrahim DN, Haris PI et al (2023), Diabetes Therapy
- In Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell: 5,554 adults with type 2 diabetes in 12 observational studies from Middle Eastern and Asian countries (n=12 studies (5,554 people)). HbA1c and fasting blood glucose were significantly lower after Ramadan than before it (heterogeneity high, about 93% and 81%); body weight did not change. The authors call the outcomes favourable and say effects of diet, activity and sleep need study. No study looked only at young adults.

## Interventions for people with type 2 diabetes mellitus fasting during Ramadan
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/lee-2023-37435938/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37435938/
Citation: Lee SWH, Chen WS, Sellappans R, Md Sharif SB et al (2023), Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
- In Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell: 5,359 Muslims with type 2 diabetes fasting in Ramadan, in 17 randomised trials of drugs or education (n=17 trials (5,359 people)). Every trial had at least one high-risk domain for bias. Dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 inhibitors may cause less hypoglycaemia than sulphonylureas (low-certainty evidence). The evidence on serious hypoglycaemia, other harms and HbA1c was very uncertain, and no deaths were reported. Trials compared medicines; none tested whether fasting itself is safe.

## The effect of intermittent fasting on the clinical and hematological parameters of patients with sickle cell disease: A preliminary study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/ahmed-2023-36895718/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36895718/
Citation: Ahmed K, Abdu Y, Khasawneh S, Shukri A et al (2023), Frontiers in Medicine
- In Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell: 52 adult Muslims with sickle cell disease in Qatar (about 70% Arab, the rest African or Asian; 90% HbSS) who fasted in Ramadan 2019 to 2021 (n=52). The numbers of severe vaso-occlusive crises and haemolytic crises did not differ significantly before, during or after Ramadan. Platelet count, reticulocyte count and creatinine did differ. The authors call it preliminary and say larger studies are needed.

## Predictors and health impacts of Ramadan intermittent fasting among patients with sickle cell disease
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/alsalman-2025-40510850/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40510850/
Citation: Alsalman MH, Alsalman Z, Alshams MM, Aljasem JM et al (2025), Frontiers in Medicine
- In Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell: 320 adult Muslims with sickle cell disease in Saudi Arabia (67% fasted) (n=320). A history of crises, emergency visits, acute chest syndrome or intensive care admission made fasting the whole month less likely. People with more than four episodes or more than four emergency visits in a year had higher odds of complications in the 30 days after Ramadan. The authors say effects are subtle during the month and larger afterwards.

## Intraday blood rheological changes induced by Ramadan fasting in sickle cell trait carriers
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/diaw-2013-23915011/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23915011/
Citation: Diaw M, Connes P, Samb A, Sow AK et al (2013), Chronobiology International
- In Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell: 20 African male students in Senegal: 10 with sickle cell trait and 10 with normal haemoglobin (n=20). Blood viscosity rose markedly in the evening in the people with sickle cell trait during Ramadan, and not in the normal-haemoglobin group, which the authors say indicates higher risk of impaired blood flow in small vessels. Plasma glucose was lower in both groups during Ramadan. They call for specific medical recommendations for trait carriers who fast.

## Changes in glycemic control and blood pressure during the Assumption Fast in Ethiopian Orthodox Christians with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a prospective observational study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/gichamo-2026-41618296/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41618296/
Citation: Gichamo FG, Mulisa MD, Regasa ND, Dadi MA et al (2026), BMC Endocrine Disorders
- In Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell: 68 Ethiopian Orthodox Christians with type 2 diabetes, fasting the Assumption Fast in Addis Ababa (n=68). Mean fasting blood glucose fell by 19.56 mg/dL and systolic and diastolic blood pressure by about 9 mmHg; the share in the glucose target range rose from 67.6% to 91.2%. The authors say larger trials with follow-up are needed.

## Dietary glycemic index and load in relation to risk of uterine leiomyomata in the Black Women's Health Study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/radin-2010-20200259/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20200259/
Citation: Radin RG, Palmer JR, Rosenberg L, Kumanyika SK et al (2010), American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
- In Fibroids, food and supplements: 21,861 premenopausal Black women in the Black Women's Health Study, followed 1997-2007 (n=21861). During 162,604 person-years, 5,800 fibroid cases were diagnosed. Dietary glycaemic index was weakly associated with fibroid risk overall (highest against lowest quintile 1.09, 95% CI 0.99-1.19; P for trend 0.04), with stronger links in women under 35 for glycaemic load (1.18) and in college-educated women for glycaemic index (1.17).

## Effect of Oral Consumption of Vitamin D on Uterine Fibroids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/alsharif-2024-38234246/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38234246/
Citation: Alsharif SA, Baradwan S, Alshahrani MS, Khadawardi K et al (2024), Nutrition and Cancer
- In Fibroids, food and supplements: 511 women with fibroids in 5 randomised trials of oral vitamin D (256 treated, 255 on placebo) (n=5 trials (511 people)). Vitamin D supplementation significantly decreased fibroid size (standardised mean difference -0.48, 95% CI -0.66 to -0.31) and raised serum vitamin D, with a larger effect in trials lasting more than 8 weeks. The authors say larger well-designed trials are needed for other outcomes.

## Treatment of symptomatic uterine fibroids with green tea extract: a pilot randomized controlled clinical study
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/roshdy-2013-23950663/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23950663/
Citation: Roshdy E, Rajaratnam V, Maitra S, Sabry M et al (2013), International Journal of Women's Health
- In Fibroids, food and supplements: 39 women aged 18-50 with symptomatic fibroids (33 completed), Egypt (n=39). Fibroid volume fell significantly in the green tea extract group (22 women) while it rose 24.3% in the placebo group (11 women). Symptom severity fell 32.4%, quality of life improved 18.5%, haemoglobin rose 0.7 g/dL and monthly blood loss fell from 71 to 45 mL. No adverse effects were observed.

## High cumulative incidence of uterine leiomyoma in black and white women: ultrasound evidence
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/baird-2003-12548202/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12548202/
Citation: Baird DD, Dunson DB, Hill MC, Cousins D et al (2003), American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
- In Fibroids: symptoms, treatment and pregnancy: 1,364 randomly selected women aged 35-49 in a US urban health plan (Black and White) (n=1364). By age 50, cumulative incidence of fibroids was above 80% for Black women and nearly 70% for White women (odds ratio 2.9, 95% CI 2.5-3.4). Fibroids developed at earlier ages in Black women. Fifty-one percent of premenopausal women with no previous diagnosis had ultrasound evidence of fibroids.
- In Iron, heavy periods and fibroids: 1,364 randomly selected women aged 35-49 in a US urban health plan (Black and White) (n=1364). By age 50, cumulative incidence of fibroids was above 80% for Black women and nearly 70% for White women (odds ratio 2.9, 95% CI 2.5-3.4). Fibroids developed at earlier ages in Black women. Fifty-one percent of premenopausal women with no previous diagnosis had ultrasound evidence of fibroids.

## Racial disparities in uterine fibroids and endometriosis: a systematic review and application of social, structural, and political context
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/katon-2023-36682686/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36682686/
Citation: Katon JG, Plowden TC, Marsh EE (2023), Fertility and Sterility
- In Fibroids: symptoms, treatment and pregnancy: US studies of fibroids and endometriosis in Black and White women (n=not stated in the abstract). Prevalence of fibroids was consistently higher in Black than in White women, with the size of the difference varying by population and case definition. Black women with fibroids or endometriosis experienced worse clinical and surgical outcomes. The authors link the disparities to differing exposures, poor access to highly skilled gynaecologic surgeons, and bias within health care.
- In PCOS, endometriosis and heavy periods: US studies of fibroids and endometriosis in Black and White women (n=not stated in the abstract). Prevalence of endometriosis varied considerably with population and case definition but was the same or lower in Black than White women. Data suggest no racial difference in incidence of endometriosis. Black women with fibroids or endometriosis had worse clinical and surgical outcomes. The authors link disparities to exposures, access to skilled surgeons and bias.

## Disparities in dermatology AI performance on a diverse, curated clinical image set
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/daneshjou-2022-35960806/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35960806/
Citation: Daneshjou R, Vodrahalli K, Novoa RA et al (2022), Science Advances
- In Finding a dermatologist who knows dark skin: 656 skin images (207 Fitzpatrick V-VI) in the Diverse Dermatology Images dataset; dermatologists and AI (n=656). AI models did worse on Fitzpatrick V-VI than I-II (for example ROC-AUC 0.55 against 0.64 for ModelDerm, with overlapping 95% intervals of 0.46 to 0.64 and 0.55 to 0.70; DeepDerm 0.50 against 0.61, HAM10000 0.57 against 0.72; figures from the full text, PMC9374341, opened 12 Nov 2026); dermatologists were also worse on dark skin; fine-tuning on the dataset closed the AI gap.

## Representations of race and skin tone in medical textbook imagery
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/louie-2018-29501717/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29501717/
Citation: Louie P, Wilkes R (2018), Social Science and Medicine
- In Finding a dermatologist who knows dark skin: 4,146 images from four core US medical textbooks (n=4146). 74.5% of images showed light skin, 21% medium and 4.5% dark.
- In How skin conditions look on dark skin (redness, rashes, rosacea, sunburn): 4,146 images from four core US medical textbooks (n=4146). 74.5% of images showed light skin, 21% medium and 4.5% dark.

## Prevalence of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency in U.S. Army personnel
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/chinevere-2006-17036616/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17036616/
Citation: Chinevere TD, Murray CK, Grant E, Johnson GA (2006), Military Medicine
- In G6PD deficiency: who carries it and what to avoid: 63,302 US military personnel tested for G6PD, October 2004 to January 2005 (54,874 males, 8,428 females) (n=63302). 2.5% of males and 1.6% of females were deficient, most with only moderate deficiency. African American males (12.2%) and females (4.1%) and Asian males (4.3%) had the highest rates. The authors judged universal screening warranted, particularly for male service members who report African American, Asian or Hispanic ethnicity.

## Epidemiology of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency in 10 malaria-endemic countries in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/taleb-2025-40225210/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40225210/
Citation: Taleb M, Brahim AT, Yebouk C, Khairy T (2025), Pan African Medical Journal
- In G6PD deficiency: who carries it and what to avoid: Studies of G6PD deficiency prevalence in the ten African countries most affected by malaria, 2000 to 2023 (n=19). Prevalence ranged from under 1% to 23.9%, more in men than in women. Antimalarials such as primaquine can cause severe haemolytic anaemia in G6PD-deficient people; the authors say prescribing should consider G6PD status and that several regions need to review diagnostic and screening protocols.

## Expanded Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium Guideline for Medication Use in the Context of G6PD Genotype
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/gammal-2023-36049896/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36049896/
Citation: Gammal RS, Pirmohamed M, Somogyi AA, Morris SA et al (2023), Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics
- In G6PD deficiency: who carries it and what to avoid: Medicines previously implicated as unsafe in G6PD deficiency (n=not stated in the abstract). Medications are classed high, medium or low-to-no risk. High-risk drugs should be avoided, medium-risk drugs used with caution, and low-to-no-risk drugs given with standard precautions. The guideline replaces the earlier rasburicase guideline.
- In Haemoglobin and white cell ranges on your blood test: listed as a source, no finding recorded.

## The association between ethnicity and care pathway for children with emotional problems in routinely collected child and adolescent mental health services data
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/edbrooke-childs-2016-26345326/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26345326/
Citation: Edbrooke-Childs J, Newman R, Fleming I et al (2016), European Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
- In Getting a child mental health support: 11,592 children from 26 CAMHS services, England (n=11,592). Children from Black and minority ethnic backgrounds were more likely to be referred to child and adolescent mental health services through education, social and other services than through primary care, compared with White British children (odds ratios 1.52 to 9.96), and less likely to end treatment for non-attendance. The authors say this may mirror the adult pattern of more compulsory than voluntary routes.

## Variations in primary open-angle glaucoma prevalence by age, gender, and race: a Bayesian meta-analysis
URL: https://vilivity.com/studies/rudnicka-2006-17003413/
PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17003413/
Citation: Rudnicka AR, Mt-Isa S, Owen CG, Cook DG et al (2006), Investigative Ophthalmology and Visual Science
- In Glaucoma and eye tests: 46 studies of open-angle glaucoma prevalence: 103,567 participants, 2,509 cases (n=103567). Black populations had the highest prevalence of primary open-angle glaucoma at all ages, though the proportional rise with age was steepest in white populations.
